findings.claim: The whole-board card width is a live function of bg.size.height, and that height is NOT latched: the toolbar's FlowLayout row count and the demo bar's wrapping headline both change mid-deal in BOTH directions, so once the shrink is engaged the entire board (foundations, free cells and all 52 cards) rescales up and down again inside the caller's withAnimation. Concretely: the 'Finish' pill is conditionally inserted mid-list in the toolbar (ContentView.swift:275-277) whenever canOfferFinish flips (Game.swift:739-742) - which happens in exactly the endgame where shrinkLatchCount is still holding the board shrunk from an earlier long column - and FlowLayout's height is row-count-driven (Extras.swift:13,18), so adding/removing a ~70pt pill can add or drop a whole ~40pt row and move totalH by that much. Same channel via demoBar's Text(demoHeadline) with .fixedSize(horizontal:false, vertical:true) (ContentView.swift:507-510), whose string changes on every demo step and whose available width changes when Pause->Resume/Next appear. The comment at ContentView.swift:108-114 argues only that the chrome is card-size-INDEPENDENT (true, and I verified there is no feedback loop) - that rules out oscillation but not a non-monotone input, which is precisely the board pulsing the shrinkLatchCount latch exists to prevent. CONFIRMED that totalH is an unlatched input and that both producers vary mid-deal; SUSPECTED (needs a device/simulator run) whether the row count actually flips on any specific device+deal. Cheap fixes: latch totalH the same way tallest is latched, or quantise the returned width into ~4pt buckets so small totalH deltas do not move it.
findings.note: Pre-existing channel (the old tableau-only shrink read the same varying height as maxH), but this commit widened the blast radius from the tableau to the whole board. Not a feedback loop - do not answer this with the feedback-loop argument, answer it with a latched or quantised width.

findings.claim: The RL-1 hardening pinned contiguous case bodies for F and C only; the iOS G, T and X token bodies are still matched by nothing that constrains their field indices or their destinations, so a one-sided iOS drift in three of the five tokens ships with CI fully green. The web copy pins case 'F'/'G'/'C' (ios-parity.test.mjs:104-110), so the guard is one-directional for G, and T/X are unpinned on both sides. Failure mode: a drifted G/T/X makes a baked winning line fail to apply on iOS, demoAdvance's guard fires, and 'Show me how to win' silently re-deals mid-line for the user while the suite stays green.
findings.note: MUTATION-VERIFIED, not eyeballed: I applied five single-token mutations to a copy of Game.swift and re-ran node --test tests/ios-parity.test.mjs each time. All five stayed 11 pass / 0 fail - (a) case G 'let idx = n(1)' -> n(2); (b) case G's up/down assignment corrupted; (c) case T 'tableau[dst].append(contentsOf: run)' -> tableau[src]; (d) case T 'let src = n(1), idx = n(2), dst = n(3)' -> n(3)/n(2)/n(1); (e) case X 'tableau[dst].append(c)' -> tableau[0].append(c). Fix is the same shape as the F/C fix: add the contiguous case "G" / case "T" / case "X" bodies to the same pin array (they match the current normalised source verbatim).

findings.claim: The drift-guard re-pin dropped coverage: nothing asserted that the F token reads its column from field 1, so an edit changing F (or C) to read n(2) would keep all pins green while making the iOS demo replay a baked line differently from index.html and tools/solver.
findings.note: VERIFIED FIXED BY MUTATION, not by reading. The pins are now contiguous normalised case bodies. F-only mutation (case "F" 'let col = n(1)' -> n(2), C untouched) => 10 pass / 1 fail. C-only mutation (case "C" only) => 10 pass / 1 fail. Baseline 11/11 green; full npm test 68/68 green. The exact hole this finding described is closed. Residual coverage gap for the OTHER tokens is tracked separately as test/ios-parity.test.mjs:g-t-x-token-bodies-unpinned.

findings.claim: The 'web demo exit paths re-deal' test claimed to pin the iOS finishDemo boardComplete guard but only asserted the demoPill wiring, so deleting Game.swift's boardComplete or applied guards left the suite green and the iOS half of the scoring-integrity rule could silently regress.
findings.note: VERIFIED FIXED BY MUTATION. Deleting Game.swift:865 'guard boardComplete else { restartDeal(); return }' => 10 pass / 1 fail; deleting Game.swift:853 'guard applied else { restartDeal(); return false }' => 10 pass / 1 fail. findings.claim: The unconditional .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) added to fix the shrunk-tableau margin also centred the tableau in the ordinary NON-shrunk case, offsetting tableau column 0 from the foundations' left edge by ((width-40) mod 8)/2 (3.5pt on 375, 3pt on 390) on every portrait deal.
findings.note: VERIFIED FIXED, and the condition is the right one. Line 130 is now .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: w < cardW ? .center : .leading). Scope-checked: the `cardW` in that ternary resolves to the body-level `let cardW` (ContentView.swift:70) = portraitCardW in portrait, not to any shadowing parameter, and portraitFitCardW returns min(widthCardW, fit) so w <= cardW always - the predicate is exactly 'shrink is active'. In the unshrunk case .leading reproduces the pre-RL-2 GeometryReader .topLeading placement, i.e. zero offset.

findings.claim: The card-size shrink applies to the tableau only: the tableau hugged the leading edge leaving a dead right margin, and w was recomputed from the live tallest column every body pass so single moves re-scaled all 52 cards and the board pulsed.
findings.note: The split-size half is GENUINELY FIXED and the arithmetic checks out; one named residual remains. Verified: (a) portrait now derives ONE width and passes it to both upperArea (:120) and tableauArea (:126); I grepped the portrait branch and no path still uses the unshrunk cardW for a card - winOverlay and demoBar draw no cards, dropZone frames are backgrounds of the already-shrunk views - so matchedGeometryEffect flights between a free cell and the tableau are now same-size. (b) The 32pt chrome constant is derived correctly, not guessed: upperArea height = groupLabel (10pt SF ~= 12) + 4 spacing + 2*cardH + 4 inter-row gap, plus the 12pt VStack gap = 32 + 3*cardAspect*w, matching units = 3*cardAspect + 0.53*(tallest-1). Fixed-size .system(size:) fonts do not scale with Dynamic Type, so the 12 is stable. (c) Estimate error is genuinely absorbed and lands in the right place: the VStack gives upperArea its natural height FIRST and the inner GeometryReader the remainder, so any chrome misestimate shifts only the tableau's maxH, and column()'s fan compression takes it - the upper row can never be clipped by fit error. Hand-checked 375x667 (totalH ~426 after a 4-row toolbar): tallest 13 -> fit 34, resulting fan floor((280.3-56.9)/12)=18 vs the 0.53*34=18.02 target; tallest 15 -> 31; tallest 18 -> the 30pt clamp binds and the fan drops to 14 (<0.53w, the known degenerate case). With the daily HUD up (totalH ~364) tallest 13 already hits the 30pt clamp. (d) Landscape regression check on removing the shrink from tableauArea: it is provably a no-op - when cardW = min(widthCardW, heightCardW) the old guard cardW*(aspect+0.53(n-1)) > maxH can never hold because the real landscape fan unit is 0.34*aspect = 0.5687 > 0.53, and when the max(30,...) clamp binds the old code returned 30 too. RESIDUAL (unchanged from round 2, item 1): every NEW column maximum still re-scales the whole board inside the caller's withAnimation, and the blast radius is now larger - a 13->14->15 column on a 375x667 phone re-flows all 52 cards AND the foundations/free cells three times on three ordinary single-card moves. Quantising the returned width into ~4pt buckets still fixes it. If that re-flow is the accepted trade, say so and I will flip this to wontfix.
